correctness.rationale: For each rank k, induced subgraphs are either independent or K_{i,j}; counting domain/range pairs and automorphisms gives an exhaustive exact polynomial. c2 fixes n and the unordered reflected products m, K-m; c3 is a function of c2 and n. Polynomial expansion yields c4(n,m)-c4(n,K-m)=(2/3)(n-2)t(8t^2-n(n-1)), t=m-K/2. If both candidate products represent bipartitions then |t|<=n/4, forcing second factor strictly negative for n>=4. Thus c4 fixes the product, and n and m fix unordered part sizes; an infinite reflected-product family proves sharpness. Direct finite enumeration independent of the polynomial formula passes for five small bicliques, plus bounded sharpness and injectivity tests. Finite enumeration is supporting evidence only.

originality.rationale: Full arXiv:1809.04422 preprint was inspected at the relevant inverse-semigroup and classification statements. Its low-rank determination concerns the ACTUAL rank-two partial bijections and their joins, whereas the claimed sharp cutoff uses only cardinalities of rank strata; the distinction is certified by nonisomorphic bicliques with identical counts through rank three. Indexed published results on homogeneous graph rank spectra and multipartite square-zero submonoids do not visibly imply arbitrary unbalanced biclique reconstruction. Their complete repository texts were inaccessible, a nonzero unresolved priority risk. No decisive covering claim was found in the actual published-finding corpus/primary searches; originality is a scoped best-knowledge assessment, not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: Full texts of the two relevant published repository records could not be read; hidden appendices or unstated corollaries may contain relevant rank formulas or equivalent inverse cutoffs.
Other unindexed earlier work may already imply the four-point reconstruction from general induced-subgraph profile formulas.
A general full-monoid reconstruction theorem does not cover the scalar-coefficient claim, but future literature review might find a stronger numerical-spectrum theorem.

value.rationale: The rank-size spectrum is a natural coarse inverse-semigroup invariant. The theorem gives a uniform exact sharp inverse threshold throughout all two-part bicliques, identifies why the third rank is redundant, and shows a genuinely infinite family of nonisomorphic objects invisible below the fourth rank. This is a structural reconstruction theorem and a complete census, not an arbitrary isolated numerical slice; its limitations to bicliques are explicit.
